title: HYDRON HAPS: HAPS-BASED OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.242) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be verified. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

description: This activity aims to provide a key enabling tool to support the design and implementation planning of ESA's Distributed Space Weather Sensor System (D3S). The first part of the activity focuses on the development of a generic end-to-end mission simulator capableof assessing the performance of distributed space weather sensing architectures. The second part leverages the developed simulator to investigate and optimise the design of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellation for space weather monitoring. Finally, the activity will assess and trade off different implementation options for the proposed constellation, including alternative payload configurations, dedicated satellites, and hosted payload opportunities
